correctness.rationale: The proof handles all quantified mixed patterns, all starts including zero, positive step and finite length, all moduli q>=2, arbitrary sufficient binary widths, and unbounded supremum. Padding invariance follows because the first one after the maximal zero prefix pins any crossing occurrence. Bit complement maps occurrences bijectively. Exactly one optional occurrence can arise from zeros preceding a reflected leading-ones expansion, and precisely for mixed v=1^r0^s. The resulting exact count identity supplies reversed color words with a constant shift and proves both directions. Actual standalone package verifier checks all 240 mixed words through length 7, 61,440 point identities, and 4,800 progressions; it is not substituted for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The mixed-pattern case is a specific explicit open question in Sobolewski (arXiv:2204.05287, p.26 Problem 4), not a manufactured subcase. The uniform finite-reflection correspondence proves the conjectured equality for all positive differences and strengthens the parity case to every residue modulus. A structural involution on arbitrary finite progressions can be reused in further questions about automatic pattern-count colorings. Neither a specific extremal length nor an arbitrary numerical census is the contribution.
